channel.title: The GW Hatchet - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Republican representative talks congressional hearing tactics, policy priorities
item.description: Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas) said his aggressive questioning in congressional hearings is designed to build public pressure for legislation.

item.title: SBA senators raise concerns over delayed student organization funding reimbursements
item.description: Student Bar Association leaders said reimbursement delays from University administrators have left some students out thousands of dollars as they await repayment for student organization expenses they paid out of pocket.

item.title: GW alum makes Israel’s World Baseball Classic roster
item.description: Former pitcher Harrison Cohen, who graduated in 2022, will compete for Team Israel at next month's World Baseball Classic.

item.title: Milken launches interdisciplinary minor, opens dual-degree programs to all students
item.description: A new interdisciplinary public health minor will launch in the fall and a new dual-degree program in exercise science is recruiting this semester as part of the changes.

item.title: Photo Essay: Buddhist monks finish 15-week ‘Walk for Peace’ in DC
item.description: Photo Essay: Buddhist monks finish 15-week ‘Walk for Peace’ in DC

item.title: GW asks DC court to remove race, religious restrictions on decades-old scholarship gifts
item.description: Officials filed three complaints last week asking the D.C. Superior Court to remove race and religious-based restrictions on decades-old charitable gifts for scholarships, arguing they violate civil rights law.

item.title: GW Hospital purchases land in Northeast DC
item.description: GW Hospital purchased an acre of vacant land in Northeast D.C. for $7.4 million last week, according to D.C. Recorder of Deeds records.

item.title: Buddhist monks conclude 2,300-mile peace walk with two-day visit to GW
item.description: Nineteen saffron-robed Buddhist monks wrapped up a nearly four-month, 2,300-mile walking journey at GW on Wednesday, capturing national attention with their call for peace amid political division.

item.title: University to relocate administrative offices to 2001 Pennsylvania Ave. over next two years
item.description: Seven administrative units will move from their current offices to 2001 Pennsylvania Ave., which officials purchased in 2024 for $35 million.

item.title: GW Dining announces partnership with sustainable food research collaborative
item.description: GW Dining announced a partnership with Menus of Change University Research Collaborative, a global network of colleges and universities that aims to study and encourage healthier and more sustainable eating habits at University dining halls, earlier this month.
